title: Imbalanced Medical Image Segmentation With Pixel-Dependent Noisy Labels (CLCS)
mechanism: Two-branch collaborative learning votes on pixel cleanliness with a curriculum dynamic threshold that protects minority classes, and a noise balance loss on suspected noisy pixels instead of dropping them.
adaptation: Two U-Net++ decoders on one ResNet-34 encoder; noise handling restricted to crack and inactive pixels; class-wise thresholds tuned for 0.19% crack pixels.
min_experiment: Arm: CLCS, 3 seeds on 5-fold CV. Baseline: house folds. Metric: fold-mean crack and inactive IoU. Promote if >= +0.01. About 20 GPU-h.
evidence: R: more than 3% Dice and mIoU gains on two benchmarks with different segmentation noise types (abstract).
prior_overlap: none; CPS at 5% labels was a semi-supervised use of two branches, not noisy-label selection.
